ONNX Runtime\'s XNNPACK kernels run the models in floating point quicker on many ARM processors (the voices, the cut-out, the translation); the quantised parts stay on the plain ones. Where they cannot run, the plain ones are used. The phone\'s GPU and NPU cannot be used: ONNX Runtime has no GPU provider on Android, and NNAPI takes only fixed shapes. Turn off if a model gives wrong results or is slower: the speed test of the subtitles tells.

Line up clips, trim and split them, add texts, pictures, sounds and subtitles, and bring anything to life with keyframes. Every change shows in the preview at once.
Two small AI models can work right on the phone. You download them with your browser and import them; the app checks every file before using it.
Every word you say, written right on time
Captions word by word, styled as you like, or a transcript as .srt or .txt that you can read and correct while it plays.
The background of a photo goes away in a tap: clean stickers, overlays and keys.
Set them up when I finish
The smart features page opens at the end of the tour. It is always in the settings too.
FFmpeg GUI has no internet permission at all: it could not go online even if it wanted to.
Files are read, edited and written on the phone. Nothing is ever uploaded.
Projects and smart models stay in the app\'s own space, out of other apps\' reach.
No accounts, no ads, no tracking
Nothing to sign up for, nothing that watches what you do.
Every line of the app can be read on GitHub.

resources.string: Choose how the picture becomes shapes. Once you edit them, the trace stays as it is.
Tap a shape to select it. Tap it again to reach the one underneath, and so on.
Drag the selection to move it: it snaps to the edges and middles of the others and of the page. Round corners size it, the pills on its sides stretch it one way, the spinning handle turns it.
Two fingers away from the selection zoom and move the drawing. The pill in the corner fits it back.
At the bottom: add shapes, texts and lines, or draw curves with the pen. With something selected, the bar changes its look, copies, reorders and deletes it. The round button lists every layer.
Turn on Pick several and tap shapes, then open More tools: join them, cut one out of another, keep where they meet, line them up, group them, make a text into shapes.

Symmetry draws on two, four or up to 24 sides at once, as a mirror or a kaleidoscope, with a grid to snap to. More tools also repeat the selection in a row, a grid or round the centre, mirror a copy beside it, simplify, smooth, reverse, break apart or join paths, and lock what should stay put.
Drag an end of a line onto a shape: it holds on to it and follows it when the shape moves.
Tap the line anywhere to add a point there. Tap a point to pick it and drag it; tap a diamond to pick the segment it sits on.
The last point of an open line
The last point joins the first: the shape can be filled
Or drag its two round handles on the stage for any curve.
Tap to place each point of a line. Tap the first point again to close it into a shape.
Tap a space surrounded by lines or shapes to fill it with the colour. If the colour runs out, close bigger gaps.
Drag an end onto a shape to connect it: it snaps to the shape\'s corners, the middles of its sides and its centre, or holds where you let go.
The top of the list is drawn on top. Drag a layer by its handle to put it above or below the others, or into a group.
